title: Server adapter layer
responsibility: Be the only door from application code into `lib/`. Each module begins with `import 'server-only'`, re-exports by explicit name or wrapper rather than `export *`, and exposes only the capabilities the shell needs; process-spawning, locking and stateful modules pass through individual review before they are exposed at all.
notes: ⚠️ PLANNED, NOT BUILT (2026-08-27). `implementedBy` is absent, and its absence is the only signal in this artifact that says so — the same convention CMP-0011 established, and the same hazard QST-0015 named: creating these records takes the orphan count to zero while nothing exists. 'Every requirement traces to a component' becomes true; 'the shell works' does not. ⚠️ THE GUARD CANNOT LIVE IN `lib/`, which is why this component exists rather than a one-line edit. AST-0033 measured that `server-only` throws when imported outside the RSC compiler, and `lib/` is imported by every `bin/` command and the whole test suite — marking it would guard the application by breaking the tool. ⚠️ IT PREVENTS NOTHING THE BUILD DID NOT ALREADY PREVENT. Both client-import cases already fail; what the marker buys is a LOCATABLE failure. Unguarded, Turbopack reports an internal error with `location: undefined` and no filename (AST-0032). ⚠️ OUTSIDE ITS BOUNDARY: it holds no logic of its own. A wrapper that adapts a signature is permitted; a wrapper that decides anything belongs in `lib/`, where the tool and the app share it. ⚠️ BUILT 2026-08-27 BY TSK-0004, and all three of its criteria now PASS — the first component of the shell to be accepted rather than merely coded. `implementedBy` says code exists; ACC-0025, ACC-0026 and ACC-0027 passing is what says it works, and the two statements are separate on purpose (QST-0015). ⚠️ THE SURFACE IS TWO MODULES AND IT IS DELIBERATELY SMALL: content-root resolution, the lint context builders, `lintProject`, stage definitions, `loadStageAttestations` and `evaluateStageGate`. Nothing that locks, writes, spawns or holds state. `evaluateHandoffGate` is absent too — publication readiness is not something a view needs to compute. ⚠️ THE CASE THAT JUSTIFIES THE NO-WILDCARD RULE IS REAL AND IS IN THIS DIRECTORY. `loadStageAttestations` and `writeStageAttestation` are exports of the SAME module, and only the first is a read. `export * from "../../lib/attestations.mjs"` would have exposed a lock-taking capability silently, on a line nobody would have read twice. A test now forbids that export by name.
